comparison: Perfect agreement on claims C3, C4, C40, C41, C42. Both OpenEval and peer reviewers find the empirical findings of nonlinearity and asymmetry in recalibration effects well-supported by experimental data. Both cite statistical support and appropriate experimental design.

Perfect agreement on claims C63, C64, C65, C81. Both evaluations accept the mechanistic explanation that modality-specific precision differences drive asymmetry patterns. Peer reviewers acknowledge this as a strength of the model without challenge.

Perfect agreement on claims C43, C44, C45, C46, C47. Both evaluations accept the core model assumptions including the double-exponential distribution for temporal perception. Peer reviewers describe methods as well-described and theoretically grounded.

Strong agreement on claims C57-C62 regarding model simulations and parameter sensitivity. Both evaluations accept these simulations as informative about model mechanisms. Peer reviewers acknowledge the demonstration of conditions under which recalibration persists at long delays.

Strong agreement on claims C8, C51, C52, C56 regarding model comparison results. Both find the causal-inference model superiority well-supported. Peer review also addresses C67 (main theoretical conclusion), accepting the evidence for causal inference role in recalibration.

Agreement on claims C82, C83, C84, C85 regarding individual differences. Both evaluations accept the explanation via individual differences in sensory precision parameters. Peer reviewers note the modeling appropriately embraces individual differences after revisions provided individual subject data.

Agreement on claims C76, C77 regarding rejection of asynchrony-correction model. Both evaluations accept this model's poor performance, though peer reviewers note the failure was somewhat predictable by design.

Significant disagreement on claims C53, C54, C55 (and related C71, C73, C78). OpenEval finds model predictions well-supported, but peer reviewers raise critical concerns that the causal inference model fails to predict behavioral data at large discrepancies, where data don't decay to zero as model predicts.

Partial disagreement on claims C9, C68, C69, C70 regarding main theoretical conclusions. OpenEval finds these well-supported, but peer reviewers express concern about limited conceptual advance, questioning whether extending causal inference to temporal domain represents major contribution beyond confirming expected parallels with spatial recalibration.

Disagreement on claims C110, C111, C112 regarding sample size. OpenEval finds the sample size (n=9) appropriate for the intensive within-subjects design. Peer reviewers consistently flag the limited sample as a weakness, with multiple reviewers expressing concern it is 'on the very low end' and 'rather low.'

Disagreement on claims C71, C73, C74 regarding model advantages over asynchrony-contingent model. OpenEval finds the explanation for alternative model failures mechanistically clear. Peer reviewers note the causal inference model's predictions at extreme SOAs remain problematic, undermining some discriminative claims.

Both address model simulation results, with overlap on C74. OpenEval emphasizes discriminative test between models as strength. Peer reviewers acknowledge simulations but note they predict vanishing recalibration at long delays that doesn't match observed behavior.

OpenEval finds claims C48, C49, C50 regarding modeling assumptions theoretically justified and supported by prior work. No corresponding peer review evaluation found addressing these specific modeling assumptions.

OpenEval finds claims C5, C6, C7, C26, C27, C28 describing the three competing model frameworks clearly formalized and appropriate. No corresponding peer review evaluation found specifically addressing these model framework descriptions.
OpenEval finds claim C66 regarding fixed bias parameter effects supported by control simulations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found addressing this specific parameter analysis.

OpenEval finds claims C88-C92 regarding alternative models and neural implementations supported by simulations and citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found addressing these neural implementation discussions.

OpenEval rates claims C93-C97 as UNCERTAIN, noting speculative interpretations about functional role extending beyond direct evidence. No corresponding peer review evaluation found addressing these speculative functional interpretations.

OpenEval finds claims C1, C2, C10-C17 establishing background and motivation well-supported by literature. No corresponding peer review evaluation found specifically addressing these background claims.

OpenEval finds claims C18-C25 establishing theoretical foundation for causal inference approach well-supported by citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found addressing this theoretical foundation.

OpenEval finds claims C29-C35 presenting rationale for precision vs. latency focus logically sound and clearly stated. No corresponding peer review evaluation found addressing this specific rationale.

OpenEval rates claims C98-C101 as UNCERTAIN, noting theoretical point about persistent biases is interesting but evidence is indirect and speculative. No corresponding peer review evaluation found addressing these persistent bias claims.

OpenEval finds claims C102-C109 reviewing prior work on factors influencing recalibration well-supported and accurately representing mixed literature findings. No corresponding peer review evaluation found addressing this literature review.
